questions.question: The parameter k in the KNN algorithm represents:

answers.a: Number of clusters in the dataset
answers.b: Number of nearest neighbours used for classification
answers.c: Number of features in the dataset

explanations.a: Incorrect because clustering refers to unsupervised algorithms like K-Means.
explanations.b: Correct because k determines how many nearby data points participate in majority voting.
explanations.c: Incorrect because features are attributes of the data and are not related to k.
explanations.d: Incorrect because k only specifies the number of neighbours considered for prediction.

questions.question: Which distance metric is most commonly used in KNN?

explanations.a: Incorrect because although Manhattan distance can be used, it is not the most commonly used metric in basic KNN.
explanations.b: Correct because Euclidean distance is the standard distance measure used to compute similarity between data points.
explanations.c: Incorrect because cosine similarity is mainly used in text similarity and vector space models.
explanations.d: Incorrect because Jaccard similarity is used for set comparisons rather than numeric distance.

questions.question: How does the KNN algorithm determine the class of a new data point?

answers.b: By majority voting among the nearest neighbours

explanations.a: Incorrect because regression equations are used in linear regression models.
explanations.b: Correct because the class label with the highest frequency among the k nearest neighbours is assigned.
explanations.c: Incorrect because clustering belongs to unsupervised learning algorithms.
explanations.d: Incorrect because KNN primarily uses distance-based voting rather than probability models.

questions.question: If k = 1, classification is based on:

explanations.a: Incorrect because majority voting requires more than one neighbour.
explanations.b: Correct because the closest data point alone decides the class.
explanations.c: Incorrect because weighting is used only when multiple neighbours are involved.
explanations.d: Incorrect because regression predicts continuous values, not class labels.

explanations.a: Incorrect because the Iris dataset is larger than 100 samples.
explanations.b: Incorrect because this does not match the standard dataset size.
explanations.c: Correct because the Iris dataset consists of exactly 150 samples.
explanations.d: Incorrect because no standard version of the Iris dataset contains 180 samples.

questions.question: The KNN algorithm is considered a non-parametric model because:

answers.a: It assumes the data follows a normal distribution
answers.b: It does not assume any predefined data distribution
answers.c: It estimates parameters using gradient descent

explanations.a: Incorrect because non-parametric models do not assume any specific data distribution.
explanations.b: Correct because KNN works directly with data without assuming a statistical model.
explanations.c: Incorrect because parameter estimation is typical in parametric models.
explanations.d: Incorrect because KNN is not based on neural network architecture.

questions.question: A very small value of k (for example k = 1) may lead to:

explanations.a: Incorrect because underfitting usually occurs when the model is too simple.
explanations.b: Incorrect because smaller k generally reduces bias but increases variance.
explanations.c: Correct because classification depends heavily on a single neighbour.
explanations.d: Incorrect because the number of distance calculations remains the same.

questions.question: When the number of features becomes very large, KNN suffers from:

explanations.a: Incorrect because data imbalance refers to unequal class distribution.
explanations.b: Correct because distance measures become less meaningful in high-dimensional space.
explanations.c: Incorrect because gradient explosion is related to neural networks.
explanations.d: Incorrect because regularization is mainly used in parametric models.

questions.question: The major computational disadvantage of KNN is:

answers.b: High prediction time due to distance calculations

explanations.a: Incorrect because KNN does not require an extensive training phase.
explanations.b: Correct because distances must be computed with many training samples during prediction.
explanations.c: Incorrect because labelled data is common for all supervised learning algorithms.
explanations.d: Incorrect because KNN actually performs well with small datasets.

explanations.b: Incorrect because KNN is widely used for classification as well.
explanations.c: Correct because KNN can perform both tasks depending on output type.
